title: Sheinbaum: False That an ‘Anti-Argentine Campaign’ Exists from Mexico
author: Néstor Jiménez and Alonso Urrutia
content:
_This article by Néstor Jiménez and Alonso Urrutia originally appeared in
the[July 27, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/07/27/politica/sheinbaum-
rechaza-que-desde-mexico-se-haya-financiado-una-campana-antiargentina),
Mexico's premier left-wing daily newspaper._

President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo rejected that an "anti-Argentine campaign"
exists, as the president of that country, Javier Milei, claimed, who asserted,
without presenting evidence, that the alleged campaign was financed from
Mexico, Brazil and by the Democratic Party.

Asked this Monday at her morning press conference about the statements of the
South American far-right figure, Sheinbaum Pardo responded:

> "It's false, there is no campaign against any country in the world, nor
> against any government in the world."

**She pointed out that, on the contrary, what does exist is a campaign
orchestrated from many places against our government, "but we are not in the
habit of meddling with other countries. Self-determination of peoples, and we
ask for the same: respect."**

Meanwhile, regarding the reform in Nicaragua that seeks to prevent the
participation of opposition parties in elections, President Claudia Sheinbaum
Pardo spoke out for the self-determination of peoples and for each country to
decide, while noting that she is in favor of democracy.

**" The first thing is the self-determination of peoples, what the people of
Nicaragua decide. And we are always in agreement with democracy on all
issues,"** she maintained this Monday at the National Palace.

Asked whether that is the course that should be taken in Mexico with respect
to conservative and right-wing groups, she made clear: "No, how could you
think that? Here there are elections every six years. What's more, there is
recall of mandate."

She insisted that there must be "democracy, democracy, democracy. Power of the
people, government of the people."

She added that** "each country decides, each people decides. We are in favor
of democracy, but each country has its self-determination and decides how it
organizes itself. There are other presidents who have been reelected and who
want to be reelected more times… each country decides. Europe has prime
ministers who can be reelected, reelected and reelected. Well, each country
decides."**
